1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard describes a procedure for the determination of bulk density of a representative

2 kg sample, of calcined petroleum tion to increase compaction. 1.2 The procedure

AND USE 3.1 Vibrated bulk density ( VBD ) is an indicator of calcined petroleum coke porosity which affects its suitability for use in pitch-bonded carbon applications. 3.2 WARNING - Vibrated bulk density for a sample of calcined petroleum coke is strongly dependent upon average particle size and particle size range. Bulk density tends to increase with decreasing coke particle size. A narrow particle size range for this test minimizes the possibility for variation due to skewing of the test sample towards either screen defining the sample. Particle size range tested should be agreed upon by the purchaser and the supplier.
Nore-An example of the use of VBD to characterize coke for prebacked anodes for aluminium smelting is reported by Belitskus who found particles passing through a O-59mm opening, No. 30F sieve and retained on a 0'30 mm opening, No. 50, sreve to be preferred. Other popular ranges are particles passing through a 2.36 mm opening, No. 8, sieve and retained on a 1.17 mm opening, No. 16, sieve for the continuous Soderberg anode process and particles passing through a 6.68 mm opening sieve ( equivalent to a 3-mesh Tyler Standard Series ) and retained on a 3.33 mm opening, No. 6, sieve for graphite electrode manufacture. 4. APPARATUS

3. SIGNIFICANCE

is limited to particles passing opening sieve ( equivalent to a

3-mesh Tyler Standard Series ) and retained on a 0'21 mm opening, No. 70, sieve ( equivalent to a 65-mesh Tyler Standard Series ). Further, the procedure is limited to a specific test sample having particles retained between screens having openings that differ by a factor of less than 2JFand preferably less than 2. 1.3 This procedure does not specify the method by which the 2 kg sample is obtained from a large lot of calcined coke. The procedure for obtaining the sample could include multiple sampling, breaking up particles with diameters greater than about 20 mm, and riffling. 1.4 This standard may involve hazardous materials, operations, and equipment. This standard does not purport to address all of the safety problems associated with its use. It is the responsibility of who-soever uses this standard to consult and establish appropriate safety and health practices and determine the applicability of regulatory limitations prior to use. 2. SUMMARY OF THE METHOD 2.1 The volume of 100 g of calcined and sized coke is measured after vibration and the bulk density is calculated.

4.1 Jaw Crusher - Laboratory type; jaw opening, approximately 50 by 200 mm; jaws may be set to gaps of approximately 3'2 to 12'7 mm; manganese steel jaw plates. 4.2 Roll Crusher - Laboratory type; glass hardened rolls of diameter, approximately 200 mm; roll width, approximately 150 mm; gap range from 0 to 12'7 mm.

6.3.1 CAUTION - To avoid damage to the rolls, size reduction with the roll crusher shall be limited to a maximum ratio of 4 to 1. Depending on the fraction desired, a one step reduction is often not possible from the maximum particle size in the jaw crusher product and intermediate roll setting are used. The sample is reduced to the desired mesh size using as few intermediate settings as possible (but not exceeding the 4 to 1 reduction ratio ).

5. PRECAUTIONS 5.1 Exercise care in the operation of the jaw crusher and roll crusher. Turn power off at the source when setting the gap. Wear safety glasses and keep hands clear when feeding the material. Turn power off at the source when the equipment is opened for cleaning after the grinding operation. 6. SAMPLE PREPARATION 6.1 Since the vibrated bulk density ( VBD ) method is based on packing of sized particles, the method of sample preparation can affect results due to shapes affecting packing differences in particle characteristics. OF APPARATUS 7.1 Graduated Cylinder - Since vibrator amplitude is affected by mass on the table, cut off the graduate below the pouring lip so that the mass is 215% 10 g. Sand sharp edges. With one common brand of graduated cylinder, this corresponds to an overall length of about 305 mm. Fit the graduate with a No. 8 stopper ( tight fit ).

6.3.7 After the roll gap is adjusted, remove the feeler gauge ( if used ), turn on the roll crusher motor, slowly feed 0'3 kg of the jaw crusher product through the roll crusher, and collect the sample. When more than one roll crushing step is required, regrind through smaller openings and collect the sample. Then, using the appropriate screens ( those defining the bulk density fraction ), sample receiver and cover, sieve the roll-crushed sample in the sieve shaker. With this final roll crusher setting, at least 30 percent of the coke generally shall be in the desired particle size range. 6.3.8 This setting would produce roughly equal mass of coke coarser and finer than the desired fraction provided that the starting material is sufficiently coarse. If yield is at least 30 percent and the ratio of coarser to finer product is between 0'8 and 2'0, crushing is satisfactory and the balance of the material is' fed through the roll crusher, using as many intermediate settings as required. The entire roll crusher product is consolidated and the desired fraction separated. 6.3.9 At the roll gap setting intended to maximize the final product, proceed as follows if the criteria in 6.3.8 are not met. If after one pass, the ratio of coarser to finer-than-desired coke is greater than 2'0, decrease the roll gap to 80 percent of its original value and test another 0.3 kg sample of jaw crusher product of intermediate roll crusher product, if required (if the product is just slightly too coarse, an alternative procedure is to make multiple passes through the roll crusher with the original gap setting). 6.3.10 If the ratio is less than 0'8 and the starting material is coarse enough to permit this ratio to be attained, increase the roll gap by 20 percent of its original value and retest with O-3 kg of jaw crusher product or intermediate roll crusher product, if required. If the starting material is not coarse enough to obtain this ratio for the particle size range selected for the test, disregard this restriction. 6.3.11 These procedures will result in a satisfactory sample as defined in 6.3.8 in the majority of cases. If not, adjust roll settings or make multiple adjustments passes, or both, with trial-and-error until a satisfactory composite sample is obtained from the 2 kg starting sample. Note that 0'3 kg fractions of the jaw crusher product may be discarded in their entirety if they are too fine after roll crushing. Partial consolidation of roll crusher products is not acceptable; that is, once a 0'3 kg sample of jaw crusher product has been passed through the roll crusher, it shall eithhr be consolidated in its

7.2 Vibrator - Fasten the cork ring securely with screws to the table top of the vibrator as a retainer ring for the graduated cylinder during the test. ( Drill and tap holes in the vibrator table as required ). The inner diameter of the cork ring is intentionally larger than the base width of the graduated cylinder. It is designed only to keep the graduated cylinder from vibrating off the vibrator table. 8. CALIBRATION OF APPARATUS 8.1 Graduated Cylinder Calibration Factor - Measure the distance, in millimetres, between the 90-ml and 170-ml marks on the graduated cylinder. Calibration factor ( ml/mm ) = ( 170 - 90 )/distance in mm. . Wrap a piece of masking[tape around the graduate with the 190-ml mark at the bottom of the tape. Make eight marks on the bottom of the tape equidistantly around the cylinder. These are used only for equally spacing height measurements ( not as a volume measurement base line ). 8.2 Determination of Accuracy Graduated Cylinder Using distilled water at 25& 5'C, fill the graduate to the 90-ml mark and determine the mass of water at that volume. Using a density of 0'997 g/cm3 for water, determine the true volume. Do the same at 20-ml increments up to the 170-ml mark. If the deviation at any indicated volume is greater than f0'5 ml, a table of indicated volumes versus true volumes should be made for use in computing bulk density. 8.3 Vibrator* - Using a hex wrench, unfasten the four screws that hold the vibrator table and remove the table. Loosen the cork locking screw. If the aluminium table is grounded, remove the ground wire. Turn the vibrator on its side and attach the ohmmeter to the table support and ground. Turn the core into the case ( clockwise ) until the ohmmeter registers zero ( core is touching the armature ). Back off the core ( counter clockwise ) until the
*This calibration procedure is for a Syntron Model J-IA or J-IB Jogger only. With a mass equivalent to the total mass of the cork ring, graduate, and test sample attached to the vibrator table, the procedure results in a vibration amplitude of 0'20-0.22 mm (peak at a fixed 60 Hz at a dial setting of 5 for Model J-IA or 35 for Model J-IB. To be satisfactory, other vibrator models shall be able to be calibrated to produce these vibration parameters.
